author: Mark Atwood
text:
Fixed via the bead's option-2 path (document the contract as deliberate best-effort with explicit three-failure-mode collapse). Added a '# Contract: best-effort, three failure modes collapse to None' section to compute_utc_times rustdoc at backend.rs:394-447, covering:
  1. Absent input (legitimate spec-conformant None — happy path)
  2. Transient backend failure (currently None; client cannot retry on response alone)
  3. Caller-bug malformed input (currently None; backend MAY log out-of-band)

Plus explicit backend-implementor guidance: surface transient-failure-distinction via out-of-band channels (logging/metrics), never panic on malformed tz_hint, route real transient failures through other methods that DO return Result.

Did NOT switch to Result<UtcTimes, ComputeUtcError<Self::Error>>. The bead identifies this as breaking once the trait stabilises; given the crate is 0.1.x pre-stable, the doc-only path preserves the option to switch later if real-world callers demonstrate they need the in-band distinction. The doc explicitly reserves the Result-shape as a possible future revision and points at bd:JMAP-ic0j.58 for the deliberation.

Justification for option-2 over option-1: callers that DO want to distinguish transient failures from spec-conformant absence (CalendarEvent/get inner loop in event.rs:118-128) would have to either suppress the transient error (re-collapse to None) or escalate it method-wide (block the get on every event's tz lookup). Neither matches the spec's allowance for 'utcStart/utcEnd MAY be absent'. The information loss at the trait boundary is therefore deliberate and the documentation makes it auditable.

Verified: cargo fmt clean, RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc clean (--all-features), clippy --all-features --all-targets -D warnings clean, cargo test --all-features 120+13+1 passed.
